cards.text: Solomon, David's son, is king of Israel now (2 Chronicles 1:1). Some people's to-do list says "buy stamps." Solomon's says: build a house for the Name of the LORD.

cards.question: Solomon plans to build a house for the Name of the LORD, and a royal ___ for himself.

cards.text: Big plans need big crews. Solomon drafts 70,000 porters, 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains and 3,600 supervisors, and friend, that's not a work crew, that's a whole CITY in work boots.
Then Solomon sends word to Hiram, king of Tyre. His ask is simple: do for me what you did for my dad.

cards.question: Solomon asks Hiram, king of Tyre, to do what he once did for David, when Hiram sent David ___ so David could build himself a house.

cards.text: Solomon tells Hiram what this house is for. It's dedicated to the LORD, for burning fragrant incense before Him and for setting out the showbread continuously.

cards.question: Solomon also tells Hiram about the burnt offerings at the LORD's house. How often will they be made?
Solomon tells Hiram that this way of worshiping the LORD is ordained for Israel forever.
Solomon tells Hiram the house he's building will be great. Why does he say so?

answers.text: Because God is greater than all gods
Because the kings around him had temples
Because Israel is stronger than Tyre

cards.text: Then Solomon hits the brakes on his own big plans. He asks who is really able to build a house for God.

cards.question: Solomon asks who could ever build a house for God. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Even the highest heavens cannot contain Him
No one on earth has enough gold for it
The whole land of Israel is too small

cards.text: Solomon asks who he is to build God a house, except as a place to burn sacrifices before Him. The man has over 150,000 workers lined up and he's STILL asking who he is. I love that.
Now Solomon gets to his order for Hiram. First up, he needs one special worker sent from Tyre.

cards.question: Solomon asks Hiram, king of Tyre, to send him a craftsman skilled in engraving.
Solomon says the craftsman from Tyre will work with his own craftsmen in Judah and ___.

cards.text: Next on the order: cedar, cypress and algum logs from Lebanon, since Hiram's servants know how to cut timber there. Solomon wants timber in abundance, because he says the temple will be great and wonderful.

cards.question: Solomon expects Hiram's servants to cut the timber in Lebanon with no help from his own servants.

cards.text: And Solomon isn't asking for freebies. He promises Hiram's woodcutters 20,000 measures each of four things, and friend, I've packed a LOT of cookie boxes, but never 20,000 of ANYTHING.

cards.question: Solomon promises Hiram's woodcutters 20,000 measures each of four things. What are they?

answers.text: Wheat and barley and wine and oil
Silver and gold and bronze and iron
Horses and chariots and carts and mules

cards.text: Hiram, king of Tyre, writes Solomon a letter back. And before he says one word about logs, he talks about the LORD.

cards.question: Hiram writes to Solomon about why the LORD set him over Israel as king. What reason does Hiram give?

answers.text: Because the LORD loves His people
Because David asked the LORD to
Because Solomon was the oldest son

cards.text: Then Hiram says, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth!" Friend, that's the king of TYRE, and I'd have bet my apron his letter opened with the invoice.

cards.question: Hiram says the LORD has given King David a wise son with insight and understanding.

cards.text: Hiram says he's sending Huram-abi, "a skillful man endowed with creativity." His father is a man of Tyre.

cards.question: Huram-abi's father is a man of Tyre, and his mother is a woman from the daughters of ___.
Hiram says Huram-abi, the craftsman he's sending, is only skilled at working with metal.

cards.text: Gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, wood, yarn, fine linen, every kind of engraving, and ANY design they give him. Friend, I'm a cookie stamper, and I've got exactly ONE design.

cards.question: After describing Huram-abi, Hiram turns to the deal. What does he ask Solomon to send his servants?

answers.text: A share of the temple gold

cards.question: Hiram says his men will cut as many logs from Lebanon as Solomon needs. How will Hiram get the logs to him?

answers.text: Float them as rafts by sea
Haul them on carts over land
Carry them on camels through the hills

cards.question: Hiram's log rafts will float by sea to a port, and Solomon can take the logs up to Jerusalem from there. Which port?

cards.text: Then Solomon counts the foreign men in Israel, following David's census, and finds 153,600. He makes them 70,000 porters, 80,000 stonecutters and 3,600 supervisors, the same numbers we saw at the start, and friend, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Card 13 already tells the baker that Solomon needs one special worker sent from Tyre. That makes 'True' obvious on card 14, so the only thing left to test is the word 'engraving', and a true or false card can't really test that. Either have card 13 set up the request without saying what Solomon asks for, or ask something card 13 doesn't settle, like what materials the craftsman will work with.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 18 says Solomon promises '20,000 measures each of four things.' Horses, chariots, carts and mules are counted, not measured, so the word 'measures' rules out one of the two wrong answers before the baker even reaches card 19.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'The food Solomon promised them,' calls the payment 'food.' The text lists wheat, barley, olive oil and wine (2 Chronicles 2:15), and wine and olive oil aren't food. Name what the text names, or use a word that fits all four, such as 'The wheat and barley and oil and wine he promised.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
